content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides whether Acts 2:30, pressed by the challenger's chain against the defender's link, leaves the point open, so it is doing a chain-vs-chain collision under the rule.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: one reading allows noting a verse's silence inside a chain-footing comparison; the other forbids making that silence the reason the point stays open.","why":"It makes the point underdetermined because the verse does not itself name whose body is the channel, which is the verse-level absence test the rule retires when the witnesses are a chain read together."}
